</span></span></foreignObject></g></g></g></g><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 613.91 -81.55)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:4.26em;--ltx-fo-height:0.68em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="9.46" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.46)" width="58.96"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">SPO Loss</span></span></foreignObject></g></g><g stroke-width="0.8pt"><path style="fill:none" d="M 0 -67.21 L 0 -21.07"></path><g stroke-dasharray="none" stroke-dashoffset="0.0pt" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" transform="matrix(0.0 1.0 -1.0 0.0 0 -20.52)"><path style="fill:none" d="M -3.54 4.32 C -2.9 1.73 -1.45 0.5 0 0 C -1.45 -0.5 -2.9 -1.73 -3.54 -4.32"></path></g></g><g stroke-width="0.8pt"><path style="fill:none" d="M 248.58 -67.21 L 248.58 -21.07"></path><g stroke-dasharray="none" stroke-dashoffset="0.0pt" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" transform="matrix(0.0 1.0 -1.0 0.0 248.58 -20.52)"><path style="fill:none" d="M -3.54 4.32 C -2.9 1.73 -1.45 0.5 0 0 C -1.45 -0.5 -2.9 -1.73 -3.54 -4.32"></path></g></g><g stroke-width="0.8pt"><path style="fill:none" d="M 473.55 -67.21 L 473.55 -21.07"></path><g stroke-dasharray="none" stroke-dashoffset="0.0pt" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" transform="matrix(0.0 1.0 -1.0 0.0 473.55 -20.52)"><path style="fill:none" d="M -3.54 4.32 C -2.9 1.73 -1.45 0.5 0 0 C -1.45 -0.5 -2.9 -1.73 -3.54 -4.32"></path></g></g><g stroke-width="0.8pt"><path style="fill:none" d="M 643.39 -67.21 L 643.39 -21.07"></path><g stroke-dasharray="none" stroke-dashoffset="0.0pt" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" transform="matrix(0.0 1.0 -1.0 0.0 643.39 -20.52)"><path style="fill:none" d="M -3.54 4.32 C -2.9 1.73 -1.45 0.5 0 0 C -1.45 -0.5 -2.9 -1.73 -3.54 -4.32"></path></g></g></g></svg></span>
</span></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span>Illustration of Directional Uncertainty-Based Method and Benchmark Methods for Experimental Design.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We compare our method against two decision-blind benchmarks. The first benchmark is purely prediction-focused: its experimental design criterion is based on standard prediction uncertainty (measured by the <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm), and its prediction model <math id="S3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is trained and evaluated using the squared <math id="S3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm (i.e., standard least squares). This algorithm is formally stated in Algorithm <a href="#alg3" title="Algorithm 3 ‣ Appendix A Benchmark Algorithms ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Benchmark Algorithms ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>, and the only differences between this benchmark and Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 2.2 Importance Weighted Sequential Experimental Design ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> are Line 4 and Line 12. The second benchmark represents a hybrid approach: it uses a design criterion based on directional uncertainty (normalized <math id="S3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm), but, like the first benchmark, it still relies on the squared <math id="S3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm for the training and elimination of the model <math id="S3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 3.1</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Consistency of metrics for training and elimination)</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">It is well known in machine learning that the loss used for model training should match the loss used for model elimination. A mismatch between these losses leads to biased model selection and invalidates convergence guarantees; see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Beygelzimer et al. (2009)</a>, <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al. (2023)</a></cite>. For this reason, the two benchmarks above are the only reasonable baselines that preserve theoretical guarantees.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To first compare our method with Benchmark Algorithm 1, we introduce the following mild assumption. This assumption ensures that a suboptimal hypothesis does not yield an SPO risk that is arbitrarily close to the optimal SPO risk.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para"><span id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_ERROR undefined">{assumption}</span>
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">[Optimality gap for decision risk]
There exsits a constant <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, such that <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}\geq\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}\geq\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> for any <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∖</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Assumption <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> is considered moderate not only due to the finite cardinality of the hypothesis set <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>, but also because the SPO risk <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{\text{SPO}}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{\text{SPO}}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> is typically discontinuous with respect to the predicted cost vector, which often results in a non-zero optimality gap. We provide a more detailed discussion and an illustrative example of this optimality gap in Section <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.
Given a fixed constant <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we denote the class of distributions that satisfy Assumption <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> by <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,
<math id="S3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}:=\left\{\mathcal{D}:\mathcal{R}_{\text{SPO}}(h)-\mathcal{R}_{\text{SPO}}^{*}\geq\alpha\text{ for any }h\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*}\right\}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> for any </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∖</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}:=\left\{\mathcal{D}:\mathcal{R}_{\text{SPO}}(h)-\mathcal{R}_{\text{SPO}}^{*}\geq\alpha\text{ for any }h\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*}\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math>
Within this class of distributions <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>α</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>, Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Earlier stopping time than decision-blind design) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> demonstrates that our proposed Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 2.2 Importance Weighted Sequential Experimental Design ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> has a bounded and finite stopping time to identify the best prediction model <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> for any distribution <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}\in\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}\in\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>. In contrast, we show that the decision-blind algorithms may not converge to the true optimal hypothesis.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Earlier stopping time than decision-blind design)</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Suppose that Assumptions <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Preliminaries for Theoretical Guarantees ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> and <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> hold with <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. We have the following results:</span></p>
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For Algorithm </span><a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 2.2 Importance Weighted Sequential Experimental Design ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_italic"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, for any </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, there exists a constant </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{0}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> (depending on </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">), such that for any distribution </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}\in\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}\in\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and for any </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\geq T_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\geq T_{0}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, with probability at least </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, the candidate prediction set </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> has excluded all suboptimal prediction models, i.e., </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T}\subseteq\mathcal{H}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T}\subseteq\mathcal{H}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For the decision-blind design (Algorithm </span><a href="#alg3" title="Algorithm 3 ‣ Appendix A Benchmark Algorithms ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_italic"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">), there exists a distribution of </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}\in\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>α</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}\in\mathcal{P}_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and a constant </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, such that for any </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, the probability of having some suboptimal prediction models within </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is larger than </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, i.e., with probability at least </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, there exists </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in H_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in H_{T}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, such that </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)&gt;R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)&gt;R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Earlier stopping time than decision-blind design) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> demonstrates a fundamental limitation of decision-blind algorithms. We achieved this by constructing a specific distribution where two distinct prediction models have a prediction error that is symmetric around the true conditional mean, yet these models lead to different optimal decisions. This scenario clearly shows that decision-blind algorithms, which minimize prediction error (e.g., squared <math id="S3.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss), may fail to converge to the true optimal hypothesis (i.e., the one minimizing SPO risk). This theoretical result reinforces our earlier observation regarding the misalignment between prediction and decision objectives.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Earlier stopping time than decision-blind design) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> establishes an earlier stopping time for our proposed Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 2.2 Importance Weighted Sequential Experimental Design ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, this performance gain stems from two key differences relative to Benchmark 1: the integration of the SPO loss criterion and the normalization of the prediction vector in the experimental design.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Notably, normalizing prediction vectors can independently accelerate convergence even without using the SPO loss criterion. In particular, Example <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Example 3.3 (Directional uncertainty yields an earlier stopping time under squared loss) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> illustrates that, under certain distributional settings, normalization leads to an earlier stopping time compared with the traditional decision-blind design. This improvement occurs even when the squared <math id="S3.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss is still used for model training and elimination, demonstrating that the directional-uncertainty (normalized <math id="S3.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> difference) criterion can provide benefits on its own.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_example">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Example 3.3</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Directional uncertainty yields an earlier stopping time under squared loss)</h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">In this example, we show that Benchmark 2 is better than Benchmark 1, as depicted in Figure <a href="#S3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. Specifically, Benchmark 2 in Figure <a href="#S3.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> still strategically leverages directional uncertainty (normalized <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> difference) to guide the experimental design criterion, but, unlike our proposed method, it uses the standard squared <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss for both model training and hypothesis elimination.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Suppose that there are two candidate designs <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and that we have two candidate prediction models, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The prediction values under two prediction models with designs <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> are shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Example 3.3 (Directional uncertainty yields an earlier stopping time under squared loss) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>. The distributions of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]</annotation></semantics></math> are also shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ Example 3.3 (Directional uncertainty yields an earlier stopping time under squared loss) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>. Particularly, for design <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, all three vectors <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}(x_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}(x_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}(x_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}(x_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> have the same direction. For design <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, the prediction <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}(x_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}(x_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> is in the same cone as <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]</annotation></semantics></math>, while <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}(x_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}(x_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> is in a different cone. Thus, in terms of the SPO loss, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is optimal. In terms of the squared loss, there is flexibility to control whether <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> minimizes the expected squared loss over two designs <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. As an illustration, suppose that <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> occur with equal probability, and that <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|h_{1}(x_{1})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]\|=\|h_{2}(x_{2})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|h_{1}(x_{1})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]\|=\|h_{2}(x_{2})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]\|</annotation></semantics></math>, as well as
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|h_{2}(x_{1})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]\|=\|h_{1}(x_{2})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|h_{2}(x_{1})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]\|=\|h_{1}(x_{2})-\mathbb{E}[c|x_{2}]\|</annotation></semantics></math>.
Consequently, in this example, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> have the same squared loss. As an illustration, we further assume that <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|h_{1}(x_{2})-h_{2}(x_{2})\|\geq\|h_{1}(x_{1})-h_{2}(x_{1})\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|h_{1}(x_{2})-h_{2}(x_{2})\|\geq\|h_{1}(x_{1})-h_{2}(x_{1})\|</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, in Benchmark 1, when quantifying the uncertainty using the <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm, design <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p2.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> has a higher probability of being sampled.</span></p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F8" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.05340v1/counterexample_normalization.png" id="S3.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:286/191;" width="286" height="191" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering ltx_font_italic"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_upright" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="S3.F8.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">An Example Showing the Benefit of Normalization When Using the Squared Loss for Decision-Focused Learning</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">In Benchmark 1, since <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> have the same expected squared loss, for any sufficiently large iteration <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, by the central limit theorem, the empirical re-weighted loss of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> will be approximately the same. Consequently, there exists a constant <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}=1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}=1/4</annotation></semantics></math>) such that, with probability at least <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is included in the confidence set <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. In other words, after <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> iterations, with probability at least <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, the optimal predictor <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> still exhibits a higher empirical reweighted squared loss than <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, leading to the incorrect selection of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">On the other hand, when we use the directional uncertainty, the uncertainty associated with design <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is zero, since <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}(x_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}(x_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}(x_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}(x_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> are in the same direction. In this case, the algorithm based on the directional uncertainty will select design <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> almost surely. Since <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}(x_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}(x_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> is closer to <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]</annotation></semantics></math> than <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}(x_{1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}(x_{1})</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c|x_{1}]</annotation></semantics></math>, by the central limit theorem, for any sufficiently large <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, the empirical squared loss of <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is smaller than <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and thus <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> will be excluded from the confidence set <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. In other words, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\forall\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\forall\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and any sufficiently large <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, with probability at least <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, Benchmark 2 satisfies <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T}=\mathcal{H}^{*}=\{h_{1}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T}=\mathcal{H}^{*}=\{h_{1}\}</annotation></semantics></math> with probability at least <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.  <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p4.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\square" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\square</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Example <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Example 3.3 (Directional uncertainty yields an earlier stopping time under squared loss) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a> demonstrates that utilizing the directional uncertainty criterion for experimental design yields superior performance, even when the squared <math id="S3.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss is retained as both the training and hypothesis elimination criterion. This result is attributable to a simple yet important property that the SPO loss is inherently scale-invariant with respect to the cost vector prediction.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Justifications and Examples of Assumptions</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that the convergence guarantee of Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 2.2 Importance Weighted Sequential Experimental Design ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> requires Assumption <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Preliminaries for Theoretical Guarantees ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>, while its theoretical performance advantage over benchmark methods requires Assumption <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>. In this section, we demonstrate that these assumptions are mild by providing concrete examples and simple transformations that satisfy them.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Justification of the Directional Margin Condition</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we show that for any instances of the finite hypothesis class <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>, Assumption <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Preliminaries for Theoretical Guarantees ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> can be achieved by taking a simple pre-processing step. Let us first introduce the concept of the equivalent hypothesis class.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 4.1</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Equivalent Hypothesis Class)</h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given two hypothesis classes <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and a sample space <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, we say that <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> are equivalent with respect to <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> if the following conditions hold:</span></p>
<ol id="S4.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For every </span><math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and every </span><math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, there exists </span><math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> such that </span><math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{SPO}(h(x))=R_{SPO}(\tilde{h}(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{SPO}(h(x))=R_{SPO}(\tilde{h}(x))</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For every </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and every </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, there exists </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}\in\mathcal{H}_{1}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> such that </span><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{SPO}(h(x))=R_{SPO}(\tilde{h}(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>P</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{SPO}(h(x))=R_{SPO}(\tilde{h}(x))</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The definition of an equivalent hypothesis class essentially states that for every hypothesis in the original class, there exists a corresponding hypothesis in the transformed class with the same SPO risk. Consequently, replacing a given hypothesis class with an equivalent one does not alter the fundamental optimization problem of identifying the hypothesis that minimizes the SPO risk.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Now we state the procedure of pre-processing and how it works: First, for any <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\text{conv}\{v_{1},\dots,v_{k}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>conv</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\text{conv}\{v_{1},\dots,v_{k}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we can calculate non-degenerate cost vectors <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1},\dots c_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1},\dots c_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to each cone, where <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is any vector in the interior of <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{K}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒦</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{K}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=\min_{i=1,...,k}\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(c_{i})}{\|c_{i}\|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=\min_{i=1,...,k}\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(c_{i})}{\|c_{i}\|}</annotation></semantics></math>. We then pass the original hypothesis class into Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> to obtain the augmented class <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Proposition 4.2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> shows that <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> is an equivalent hypothesis class with the desired non-degeneracy properties.</p>
</div>
