<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 4.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given the set of possible designs <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, for any hypothesis prediction model class <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> be the pre-processed class output by Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> after computing non-degenerate cost vectors <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1},...,c_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1},...,c_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=\min_{i=1,...,k}\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(c_{i})}{\|c_{i}\|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=\min_{i=1,...,k}\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(c_{i})}{\|c_{i}\|}</annotation></semantics></math>, the following two arguments hold:</span></p>
<ol id="S4.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S4.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assumption </span><a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Preliminaries for Theoretical Guarantees ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_italic"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a><span id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is satisfied with parameter </span><math id="S4.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> under </span><math id="S4.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I2.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and </span><math id="S4.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> are equivalent hypothesis classes.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Proposition 4.2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> implies that Assumption <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Preliminaries for Theoretical Guarantees ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> can be easily satisfied for any hypothesis class via the preprocessing step in Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Examples of Optimality Gap</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Section <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, we show that the optimality gap (Assumption <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>) can be used to formally establish the superior performance of our decision-focused algorithm relative to the decision-blind benchmark. We also note that, empirically, our algorithm continues to outperform the decision-blind alternative even in the absence of such a gap, as demonstrated in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2.SSS3" title="C.2.3 Empirical evidence of the Degeneracy Angle and Optimality Gap ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we present examples illustrating the existence of the optimality gap in Assumption <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> without relying on the standard well-specification assumption, namely that the optimal predictor <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> equals the conditional expectation <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]</annotation></semantics></math>. Our construction is based on three mild regularity conditions: (i) a relaxation of well-specification, (ii) a sensitivity condition for a particular experimental design, and (iii) a regularity condition on the prediction set and the polyhedral structure of the feasible decision space.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmcondition1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_condition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmcondition1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Condition 1</span></span></h6>
<div id="Thmcondition1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmcondition1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmcondition1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The minimum risk equals <math id="Thmcondition1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|\cdot])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|\cdot])</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,
<math id="Thmcondition1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\min_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)=\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|x],c)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{h\in\mathcal{H}}R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)=\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|x],c)]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The above condition is a relaxed, well-specified condition on the hypothesis class. It is less restrictive than assuming <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}(x)=\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}(x)=\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]</annotation></semantics></math>, since <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\alpha\,\mathbb{E}[c\mid x],c)=\ell_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c\mid x],c)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>SPO</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>SPO</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\alpha\,\mathbb{E}[c\mid x],c)=\ell_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c\mid x],c)</annotation></semantics></math> for any <math id="S4.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. The intuition is that any predictor proportional to the conditional expectation is also optimal under the SPO loss.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Under Condition <a href="#Thmcondition1" title="Condition 1 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, for any design <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}_{(j)}\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}_{(j)}\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> we have</p>
<table id="S4.Ex11" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex11X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex11X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x),c)-\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x),c)|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x),c)-\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x),c)|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex11X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x),c)-\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|x],c)|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x),c)-\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|x],c)|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex11Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}\left(w^{*}(h(x))-w^{*}(\mathbb{E}[c|x]\right)|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>c</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo>(</mo><mi>w</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>w</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>)</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>X</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}\left(w^{*}(h(x))-w^{*}(\mathbb{E}[c|x]\right)|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<tbody id="S4.Ex11Xb"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex11Xb.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]\left(w^{*}(h(\mathrm{X}_{(j)}))-w^{*}(\mathbb{E}[c|\mathrm{X}_{(j)}])\right)\geq 0," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]\left(w^{*}(h(\mathrm{X}_{(j)}))-w^{*}(\mathbb{E}[c|\mathrm{X}_{(j)}])\right)\geq 0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where the last inequality used the fact that <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w^{*}(\mathbb{E}[c|\mathrm{X}_{(j)}])" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w^{*}(\mathbb{E}[c|\mathrm{X}_{(j)}])</annotation></semantics></math> is the minimizer of <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\min_{w\in\mathcal{S}}(\mathbb{E}[c|\mathrm{X}_{(j)}])^{\top}w" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{w\in\mathcal{S}}(\mathbb{E}[c|\mathrm{X}_{(j)}])^{\top}w</annotation></semantics></math>. Hence, under condition <a href="#Thmcondition1" title="Condition 1 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, the difference in the risk is always non-negative conditional on any <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>. This enables us to lower bound the difference of <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> by conditioning on any specific design <math id="S4.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{X}_{(i)}\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{X}_{(i)}\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In order to further lower bound the difference of <math id="S4.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> condition on <math id="S4.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{X}_{(i)}\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{X}_{(i)}\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, we need conditions on a necessary condition of sub-optimal decisions. We first give the following definition.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Define <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> as the supremum over the norm of the set of vector <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\forall x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\forall x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}\in\mathcal{H}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}\in\mathcal{H}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, its downstream optimizer <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w^{*}(h^{*}(x))=w^{*}\left(\frac{h^{*}(x)}{\|h^{*}(x)\|}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w^{*}(h^{*}(x))=w^{*}\left(\frac{h^{*}(x)}{\|h^{*}(x)\|}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> stays the same after perturbation <math id="S4.SS2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{h^{*}(x)}{\|h^{*}(x)\|}\leftarrow\frac{h^{*}(x)}{\|h^{*}(x)\|}+v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{h^{*}(x)}{\|h^{*}(x)\|}\leftarrow\frac{h^{*}(x)}{\|h^{*}(x)\|}+v</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e.,</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">

</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Intuitively, <math id="S4.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> serves as the uniform upper bound on the magnitude for which it is safe to change the prediction without changing the output decision.
Now we can state a necessary condition for making a suboptimal decision.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmcondition2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_condition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmcondition2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Condition 2</span></span></h6>
<div id="Thmcondition2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmcondition2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmcondition2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">There exists <math id="Thmcondition2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{X}_{(i)}\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{X}_{(i)}\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="Thmcondition2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\mu}:=\mu(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\mu}:=\mu(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that</span></p>
</div>
<div id="Thmcondition2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left\|\frac{h^{*}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})}{\|h^{*}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})\|}-\frac{h^{\prime}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})}{\|h^{\prime}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})\|}\right\|&gt;\Delta,\quad\text{ for all }h^{\prime}\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*},h^{*}\in\mathcal{H}^{*}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic"> for all </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∖</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left\|\frac{h^{*}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})}{\|h^{*}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})\|}-\frac{h^{\prime}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})}{\|h^{\prime}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})\|}\right\|&gt;\Delta,\quad\text{ for all }h^{\prime}\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*},h^{*}\in\mathcal{H}^{*}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Condition <a href="#Thmcondition2" title="Condition 2 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> states that there exists a design <math id="S4.SS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{X}_{(j)}\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{X}_{(j)}\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> with strictly positive probability mass <math id="S4.SS2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\mu}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><munder accentunder="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\mu}</annotation></semantics></math> such that a suboptimal prediction leads to a suboptimal downstream decision. Combined with Condition <a href="#Thmcondition1" title="Condition 1 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, this allows us to lower bound <math id="S4.SS2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> by the objective difference induced by a suboptimal decision. To translate this decision-level distinction into a gap in SPO risk, we impose the third condition.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmcondition3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_condition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmcondition3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Condition 3</span></span></h6>
<div id="Thmcondition3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmcondition3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmcondition3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Suppose that the norm of the conditional expectation <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded below by a positive constant <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><munder accentunder="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{c}</annotation></semantics></math>, that is, <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]\|\geq\underline{c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathbb{E}[c\mid x]\|\geq\underline{c}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>. Recall the the convex hull representation of <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}=\text{conv}\{v_{1},\dots,v_{k}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">conv</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}=\text{conv}\{v_{1},\dots,v_{k}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, define the minimum distance between vertices of <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> as
<math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\gamma}:=\min_{i,j\in\{1,\dots,k\},i\neq j}\|v_{i}-v_{j}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\gamma}:=\min_{i,j\in\{1,\dots,k\},i\neq j}\|v_{i}-v_{j}\|</annotation></semantics></math> and suppose <math id="Thmcondition3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\gamma}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\gamma}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Condition <a href="#Thmcondition3" title="Condition 3 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> requires that neither the norm of the true conditional expectation nor the minimum distance between vertices of <math id="S4.SS2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is arbitrarily close to zero. Together, Conditions <a href="#Thmcondition1" title="Condition 1 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, <a href="#Thmcondition2" title="Condition 2 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, and <a href="#Thmcondition3" title="Condition 3 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> serve as mild regularity assumptions that rule out pathological or irregular distributions and are commonly satisfied in practice. We are now ready to present an example that shows how to construct an optimality gap under these conditions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 4.3</span></span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Under Conditions <a href="#Thmcondition1" title="Condition 1 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, <a href="#Thmcondition2" title="Condition 2 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, and <a href="#Thmcondition3" title="Condition 3 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, the optimality gap in Assumption <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> holds with <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=\underline{\mu}\,\eta\,\underline{c}\,\underline{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=\underline{\mu}\,\eta\,\underline{c}\,\underline{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p11.1" class="ltx_p">Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem3" title="Proposition 4.3 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> provides a concrete example ensuring the existence of a non–arbitrarily small optimality gap. Together with the analysis in Section <a href="#S3.SS1" title="3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, this optimality gap can be used to establish the superiority of our algorithm over the benchmark methods.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Numerical Study</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To illustrate the effectiveness of our approach, we conducted two sets of numerical studies: one on the cost-sensitive classification problem and another on the LLM resource allocation problem. We benchmarked:</p>
<ol id="S5.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">(Our Method)</span> Directional uncertainty with SPO loss-based model elimination/training</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> uncertainty with SPO loss-based model elimination/training</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Directional uncertainty with <math id="S5.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss-based model elimination/training</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> uncertainty with <math id="S5.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss-based model elimination/training</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Methods 1 and 2 use the SPO loss to shrink the hypothesis set, whereas Methods 3 and 4 rely on the squared <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss. The contrast between Methods 1 and 3 versus Methods 2 and 4 isolates the impact of using directional uncertainty under a fixed loss criterion.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Cost-Sensitive Classification</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The cost-sensitive multiclassification problem can be formulated as a contextual stochastic linear optimization problem, as detailed in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Application Example: Cost-Sensitive Multiclass classification ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>,. We now apply this framework to a modern clinical diagnosis setting, where a predictive model is trained to determine whether a patient has a disease based on a dataset containing objective, examination, and subjective features. If the model can accurately predict disease presence, the cost of performing precise diagnostic procedures can be avoided. At the same time, the cost-sensitive formulation explicitly accounts for the asymmetry between false negatives and false positives, thereby aligning the learning objective with the operational goal of minimizing overall diagnostic costs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We consider an experimental design setting in clinical diagnosis, where controlled experiments can be conducted on different patients to obtain their true health conditions. However, performing precise diagnostic tests is often costly. Therefore, we aim to develop an efficient data collection pipeline that enables accurate model training while minimizing experimental costs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Specifically, we used the cardiovascular disease dataset from Kaggle<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
              
              
              
              
              
              
              
            <a href="https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sulianova/cardiovascular-disease-dataset" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href">https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sulianova/cardiovascular-disease-dataset</a>. This dataset has been extensively studied in medical research; see, for example, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sadr et al. (2024)</a></cite>.</span></span></span>. In cardiovascular diagnosis, the conventional approach involves conducting an MRI test, which is precise but costly. Alternatively, a predictive model can serve as a clinical decision-support tool by estimating the likelihood of disease presence based solely on readily available patient features.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The dataset contains more than 60,000 patient records, each indicating whether the individual has cardiovascular disease. To construct the candidate hypothesis set <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>, we randomly sampled <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\in\{10,25,50,100,10000\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>25</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10000</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\in\{10,25,50,100,10000\}</annotation></semantics></math> data points from the dataset and minimized the SPO<math id="S5.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math> loss to obtain five linear predictors (linear mappings from features to labels). Each minimization was performed using stochastic gradient descent with a step size of <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\times 10^{-3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times 10^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>, a batch size of 256, and 12 epochs. In this manner, we obtained five linear predictor hypotheses, where the first four are regarded as suboptimal and the fifth as the best-performing hypothesis.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">To align with our experimental design framework, we employed the K-means clustering algorithm to identify clusters that represent distinct patient types based on empirical density. The number of clusters was set to 15. In each iteration of our algorithm, we consider the experimental design to be selecting a sample from one of the cluster centers and drew its corresponding true label from the same cluster.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, to evaluate the effectiveness of our algorithm relative to the benchmark methods, we conducted 100 trials for each method and computed the mean SPO loss on the testing set. An example illustrating the testing set loss trajectories with 95% confidence intervals of our algorithm and the benchmarks is shown in Figure <a href="#S5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 5.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, where the <span id="S5.SS1.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">cost ratio</span> refers to the ratio between unit false negative cost and false positive cost, and is set to 3 in the basic setting.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Another important consideration is how model performance changes when the objective value becomes more asymmetric in the cost of misclassification. In the cost-sensitive classification problem, this sensitivity is directly linked to the cost ratio. When the ratio is low, making accurate predictions aligns closely with making optimal decisions; when the ratio is high, this alignment weakens, and the objective becomes more sensitive to decision quality. To examine this effect, we varied the cost ratio and plotted the testing set loss ratio of our methods relative to decision-blind benchmarks after 100 iterations. Figure <a href="#S5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 5.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> presents the test-set loss ratio with 95% confidence intervals across cost ratios ranging from 1 to 15.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F10" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S5.F10.fig1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:158.7pt;"><img src="2602.05340v1/replay.png" id="S5.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:219/178;" width="219" height="178" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F10.fig1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="S5.F10.fig1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Cost-Sensitive Classification</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S5.F10.fig2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:158.7pt;"><img src="2602.05340v1/cost_ratio_loss_ci_plot_2.png" id="S5.F10.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:219/180;" width="219" height="180" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F10.fig2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="S5.F10.fig2.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">SPO Loss Ratio vs. Cost Ratio</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 5.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> reveals the following key insights:</p>
<ul id="S5.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using the SPO loss as the elimination criterion leads to a substantial reduction in loss. This can be observed by comparing the directional-uncertainty-based and <math id="S5.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>-uncertainty-based algorithms trained with <math id="S5.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss against their counterparts trained with <math id="S5.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> loss.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Incorporating directional uncertainty yields a moderate improvement, as shown by comparing the directional-uncertainty-based algorithms with the <math id="S5.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>-uncertainty-based algorithms under both <math id="S5.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.I2.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> loss criteria.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">On the other hand, Figure <a href="#S5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ 5.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> showed that, as the cost ratio increases, the performance advantage of our decision-focused method over the decision-blind benchmarks grows correspondingly.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">These results demonstrate that incorporating directional uncertainty provides consistent improvements, while minimizing <math id="S5.SS1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> better aligns the learning objective with decision-making performance. Further experimental details and results are provided in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS1" title="C.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>LLM Assignment Problem</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Section <a href="#S1.SS2" title="1.2 Application Example: Contextual Job Assignment ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a>, we demonstrated that the sequential design can also be applied to an LLM job assignment problem. Following this formulation, we conducted an experiment using collected web text data and incorporated human evaluation.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We consider a setting where text generation tasks for an input from a specific category are assigned to different LLMs. We assumed there is a consistent quality score measure for these generated texts, and our objective is to maximize this score for each generated text (see evaluation rubrics in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>.). We also assumed the text generation tasks are in a parallel setting where the tasks are not sequentially dependent, which allows us to adopt the formulation in Section <a href="#S1.SS2" title="1.2 Application Example: Contextual Job Assignment ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1.2</span></a>. We assume the hypotheses are mappings from text categories to task scores. In this way, by predicting task performance for any given text category, we can solve the assignment problem and determine an optimal allocation of the models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">In our experiment setting, we considered five tasks: text summarization, text extension, text translation, bullet point generation, and sentiment analysis. These tasks cover two main categories: condensing tasks, which reduce or analyze texts, and generative tasks, which create new text beyond the given texts. Condensing tasks are more common tasks while generative tasks requires more model knowledge and capability.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Regarding the LLMs, we used ChatGPT5, Gemma3, Qwen1.5, and Deepseek-llm. Among these models, ChatGPT5 represents the more advanced but expensive models, while the other three represent older, less powerful, and more accessible models. Reflecting this categorization, we imposed capacity constraints: ChatGPT5 was limited to a single use, while the other three models could each be used up to two times.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">To collect and label data, we gathered 50 short texts from five diverse categories: Wikipedia mathematics, Wikipedia animals, medical journal abstracts, UNC alumni news, and movie reviews. These categories were chosen to represent a wide range of text types, with different topics and tones. The generated output for each text was then assessed by human evaluators using a 1-to-5 quality scale (1=poor, 5=perfect) based on a consistent criterion. The summary of the task scores is provided in Table <a href="#A3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ C.2.1 Experiment Setup and Data Collection ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In the experiment, each prediction model was constructed by drawing bootstrap samples of size <math id="S5.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> from each category (with replacement) and taking their averages. The candidate hypothesis class <math id="S5.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> was then formed by varying <math id="S5.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\in\{1,3,5,7,10\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\in\{1,3,5,7,10\}</annotation></semantics></math>. This resampling technique was used to overcome the problem of limited data, with scores calculated as the categorical sample means. For each method, we conducted 100 trials and computed the average SPO loss and <math id="S5.SS2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> loss on the testing set, which comprises 20% of the dataset. The results are shown in Figure <a href="#S5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ 5.2 LLM Assignment Problem ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> and Figure <a href="#S5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ 5.2 LLM Assignment Problem ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F12" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S5.F12.fig1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:158.7pt;"><img src="2602.05340v1/spo_loss_curves_avg_llm.png" id="S5.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:219/183;" width="219" height="183" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F12.fig1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 11</span>: </span><span id="S5.F12.fig1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">LLM Allocation Problem SPO Loss</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S5.F12.fig2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_top" style="width:158.7pt;"><img src="2602.05340v1/l2_loss_curves_avg_llm.png" id="S5.F12.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:219/184;" width="219" height="184" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F12.fig2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 12</span>: </span><span id="S5.F12.fig2.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">LLM Allocation Problem L2 Loss</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">For decision quality, the results in Figure <a href="#S5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ 5.2 LLM Assignment Problem ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> are consistent with the cost-sensitive classification experiment. Our decision-focused algorithm with directional uncertainties outperforms other benchmarks. Moreover, Figure <a href="#S5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ 5.2 LLM Assignment Problem ‣ 5 Numerical Study ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> further highlights the fundamental mismatch between prediction and decision objectives. Although benchmark decision blind methods perform well on the <math id="S5.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> prediction metric, they fail to converge to a predictor that induces the optimal decision.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">These results from a real-world experiment demonstrate the strength of our algorithm and provide a concrete example of the mismatch induced by decision-blind algorithms. More details on the experimental setup are provided in Appendix <a href="#A3.SS2" title="C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, to address the misalignment between decision loss and traditional experimental design criteria based solely on prediction uncertainty, we propose a new uncertainty measure that captures the <em id="S6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">directional</em> uncertainty of predictions. This criterion leads to a theoretically earlier stopping time compared with decision-blind design methods. Real-world numerical experiments further demonstrate the advantages of our approach over benchmark algorithms. This directional uncertainty-based criterion provides new insights into quantifying uncertainty in the predict-then-optimize paradigm for future studies.</p>
</div>
</section>

</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock ltx_bib_cited">Cited by: <a href="#S1.SS3.p2.1" title="1.3 Related Work ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">§1.3</span></a>.

</div>
<div id="alg3.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg3.l13.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">13:</span></span>
            
            
            Update <math id="alg3.l13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{t}\leftarrow\arg\min_{h\in H_{t-1}}\hat{\ell}^{t}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{t}\leftarrow\arg\min_{h\in H_{t-1}}\hat{\ell}^{t}(h)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="alg3.l13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{\ell}^{t,*}\leftarrow\min_{h\in H_{t-1}}\hat{\ell}^{t}(h)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{\ell}^{t,*}\leftarrow\min_{h\in H_{t-1}}\hat{\ell}^{t}(h)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg3.l14" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg3.l14.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">14:</span></span>
            
            
            Update the confidence set of the predictor <math id="alg3.l14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="alg3.l14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}\leftarrow\{h\in H_{t-1}:\hat{\ell}^{t}(h)\leq\hat{\ell}^{t,*}+r_{t}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>t</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}\leftarrow\{h\in H_{t-1}:\hat{\ell}^{t}(h)\leq\hat{\ell}^{t,*}+r_{t}\}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg3.l15" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg3.l15.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">15:</span></span>
            
            
            Update <math id="alg3.l15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t+1}\leftarrow r_{t}\sqrt{\frac{t}{t+1}\frac{\log(2(t+1))}{\log(2t)}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><mfrac><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t+1}\leftarrow r_{t}\sqrt{\frac{t}{t+1}\frac{\log(2(t+1))}{\log(2t)}}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>

           <span id="alg3.l16.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg3.l16.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>
