<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Application Example: Cost-Sensitive Multiclass classification</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">One application of decision-focused learning is in the cost-sensitive multiclass classification. Let <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> denote the feature input and <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> denote the corresponding label.
Suppose there are <math id="A2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> classes and <math id="A2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> is a cost matrix with non-negative entries. Here <math id="A2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the misclassification cost for assigning a sample to a class <math id="A2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> when the true class is <math id="A2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. Assuming that a correct classification incurs no cost, then the diagonal of <math id="A2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}</annotation></semantics></math> is zero. Under this setup, for a given input <math id="A2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, the classification goal is to minimize the expected misclassification cost, i.e., <math id="A2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\min_{j\in\{1,\cdots,m\}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{P}(Y=i|X=x)\mathcal{C}_{i,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mmultiscripts><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\min_{j\in\{1,\cdots,m\}}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{P}(Y=i|X=x)\mathcal{C}_{i,j}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=[c_{1},...,c_{m}]^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=[c_{1},...,c_{m}]^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> be the binary unit vector encoding the true class label, i.e., <math id="A2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i}=1</annotation></semantics></math> if the true class of a sample is <math id="A2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{k}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{k}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\neq i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\neq i</annotation></semantics></math>. Then the expected cost of predicting the sample as class <math id="A2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> can be expressed as <math id="A2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{P}(Y=i|X=x)\mathcal{C}_{i,j}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}[c_{i}|x]\mathcal{C}_{i,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{P}(Y=i|X=x)\mathcal{C}_{i,j}=\sum_{i=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}[c_{i}|x]\mathcal{C}_{i,j}</annotation></semantics></math>. If we further use a probability vector <math id="A2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w\in\mathbb{R}^{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w\in\mathbb{R}^{m}</annotation></semantics></math> to denote the decision vector, the resulting contextual stochastic linear programming formulation of the classification problem is:</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="A2.p2.1" class="ltx_block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:138.0pt;">
<table id="A2.EGx6" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_centering ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\min_{w\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\quad" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></munder><mspace style="width:1.167em;" width="1.167em"></mspace></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\min_{w\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\quad</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[(c^{\top}\mathcal{C})w|x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[(c^{\top}\mathcal{C})w|x]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A2.Ex15"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><span id="A2.Ex15.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">s.t.</span></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{1}^{\top}w=1," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>𝟏</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{1}^{\top}w=1,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<p id="A2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">which is equivalent to

<span id="A2.p2.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:103.5pt;">
<span id="A2.EGx7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<span id="A2.Ex17"><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\min_{w,y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\quad" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>m</mi></msup></mrow></munder><mspace style="width:1.167em;" width="1.167em"></mspace></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\min_{w,y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\quad</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}y|x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>c</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}y|x]</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
<span id="A2.Ex18"><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><span id="A2.Ex18.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath">s.t.</span></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbf{1}^{\top}w=1," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mn>𝟏</mn><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbf{1}^{\top}w=1,</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
<span id="A2.Ex19"><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle y=Cw," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>w</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle y=Cw,</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
<span id="A2.Ex20"><span class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></span>
<span class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A2.Ex20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle w\geq 0." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>w</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle w\geq 0.</annotation></semantics></math></span>
<span class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></span></span></span>
</span>
</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">As an illustrative example, consider a clinical testing scenario such as cardiovascular diagnosis, where there are <math id="A2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m=2</annotation></semantics></math> classes: class 1 corresponds to negative and class 2 corresponds to positive. Suppose the cost for a false positive is 1 and a false negative is 2, then the cost matrix is <math id="A2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}=\begin{bmatrix}0&amp;1\\
2&amp;0\end{bmatrix}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn></mtd><mtd><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}=\begin{bmatrix}0&amp;1\\
2&amp;0\end{bmatrix}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Experiment Details</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Cost-Sensitive Classification Experiment Details</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section details the experimental setup and additional findings for cost-sensitive classification. All experiments were executed on a MacBook Pro (Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB RAM).</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the experiment, we first removed outliers from the dataset. Specifically, we excluded samples with systolic blood pressure greater than 250 or less than 70, and those with diastolic blood pressure greater than 200 or less than 40.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We conducted <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>100</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">100</annotation></semantics></math> independent trials of the experiment. The hyperparameter <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> minimizer are set to be 5 and 100 respectively. In each trial, <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\%</annotation></semantics></math> of the total dataset was randomly designated as the testing set. We then reported the average SPO risk on the training set, aggregated across all trials, along with its <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> confidence interval.
A subset of our experimental results is presented in Figure <a href="#A3.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ C.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">As illustrated in Figure <a href="#A3.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ C.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, when the cost ratio is 1, the objective reduces to a pure prediction task; consequently, our method yields performance comparable to benchmark approaches. However, as the cost ratio increases to 3, decision-focused methods (SPO training loss) begin to outperform decision-blind algorithms (L2 training loss) due to their alignment with the decision-making objective. Furthermore, when both methods utilize SPO training loss, our directional uncertainty algorithm demonstrates a clear advantage over the L2 uncertainty algorithm. At higher cost ratios (5, 7, 9, and 11), these trends intensify: the superiority of decision-focused over decision-blind algorithms widens, and the benefits of incorporating directional uncertainty become increasingly pronounced.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">However, as this cost ratio increases, the performance advantage of our method becomes significant, which highlights its alignment with the decision-focused objective.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">In addition to Figure <a href="#A3.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ C.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>, table <a href="#A3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ C.1 Cost-Sensitive Classification Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the experiment result by using the percentage SPO risk metric. The percentage SPO risk for a hypothesis <math id="A3.SS1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> is defined as <math id="A3.SS1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N_{test}}\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x_{i}),c_{i})-\sum_{i=1}^{N_{test}}\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x_{i}),c_{i})}{\sum_{i=1}^{N_{test}}\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x_{i}),c_{i})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msubsup><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msubsup><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><msubsup><mo maxsize="0.700em" minsize="0.700em" stretchy="true">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub></msubsup></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N_{test}}\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x_{i}),c_{i})-\sum_{i=1}^{N_{test}}\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x_{i}),c_{i})}{\sum_{i=1}^{N_{test}}\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x_{i}),c_{i})}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is the average percentage increase in SPO risk relative to the best-performing hypothesis. A low percentage SPO risk indicates that the hypothesis is performing well within the current candidate hypothesis class, whereas a high percentage implies the hypothesis is significantly sub-optimal. The results in the table confirm that the relative effectiveness of our algorithm improves as the cost ratio increases, thereby strengthening our previous conclusion.</p>
</div>

<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This section details the experimental setup and additional findings for LLM allocation. All experiments were executed on a MacBook Pro (Apple M1 Pro, 16 GB RAM).</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We first present the precise optimization formulation for the experiment. Let <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{i,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{i,j}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the binary decision variable for assigning task <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,\dots,5\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,\dots,5\}</annotation></semantics></math> to model <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\in\{1,\dots,4\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\in\{1,\dots,4\}</annotation></semantics></math>. Furthermore, let <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i,j}\in\{-5,\dots,-1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i,j}\in\{-5,\dots,-1\}</annotation></semantics></math> represent the negative performance score of the output generated for task <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> by model <math id="A3.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>; consequently, minimizing the objective function in Equation <a href="#A3.E6" title="Equation 6 ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> is equivalent to maximizing the total performance scores. Regarding constraints, Equation <a href="#A3.Ex21" title="Equation () ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">()</span> ‣ <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> defines the capacity limit for GPT-5, while Equation <a href="#A3.Ex22" title="Equation () ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">()</span> ‣ <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> governs the capacity of the remaining three models. Equation <a href="#A3.Ex23" title="Equation () ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">()</span> ‣ <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> ensures that each task is executed exactly once, and Equation <a href="#A3.Ex24" title="Equation () ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">()</span> ‣ <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.2</span></a> imposes the binary constraint on the decision variables.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle~~\sum_{j=1}^{4}w_{i,j}=1,\forall i=1...,5," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo></mstyle><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mi>w</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle~~\sum_{j=1}^{4}w_{i,j}=1,\forall i=1...,5,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">()</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A3.Ex24"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex24.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle w_{i,j}\in\{0,1\},\quad\forall i=1,...,5,j=1,...,4." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle w_{i,j}\in\{0,1\},\quad\forall i=1,...,5,j=1,...,4.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.1 </span>Experiment Setup and Data Collection</h4>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this experiment, we ran 100 independent trials, the hyperparameter <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> minimizer are set to be 5 and 20 respectively.
We used human evaluation for labeling the generated outputs. Regarding the labeling process, Table <a href="#A3.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ C.2.1 Experiment Setup and Data Collection ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> summarizes the criteria used to evaluate the generated responses, and Table <a href="#A3.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ C.2.1 Experiment Setup and Data Collection ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows the summarized statistics for the labeled output. In this collected data, we observed that the ChatGPT-5 is the most advanced model that performs well accross all tasks, while Deepseek-llm, Gemma3, Qwen1.5 have good performances only on some tasks. Among these tasks, summarization was the easiest, with a mean score of 4.55, while the other four tasks proved more challenging. The overall average score for the collected data is 3.66.</p>
</div>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Source Text:</span> (from movie ratings category)</p>
<blockquote id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3.2" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p3.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Christopher Nolan’s film *Oppenheimer* received widespread critical acclaim and exceptional audience interest. According to its Wikipedia reception summary, critics placed it near the top of year‑end lists and praised its direction, performances, and cinematography. The film became the highest‑grossing biographical feature ever and one of the top IMAX releases, reflecting sustained demand across weeks in theaters. Aggregators reported high scores, and notable filmmakers publicly lauded the work, calling it a defining achievement of the decade. The box‑office trajectory was unusual: even without immediately topping the domestic chart, it maintained momentum and ultimately crossed $900 million worldwide, with IMAX formats delivering a significant share. Taken together, the critical consensus and commercial performance position *Oppenheimer* as both a prestige title and a mainstream event, bridging awards attention with durable audience appeal.</span></p>
</blockquote>

<span id="A3.T4.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:71.1pt;">
<span id="A3.T4.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.T4.5.1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Task (Prompt)</span></span>
</span></th>
<th id="A3.T4.5.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_r ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.9pt 4.0pt;">
<span id="A3.T4.5.1.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:313.0pt;">

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.2 </span>Robustness Check Under Extra Constraint</h4>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To demonstrate our method’s robustness across different scenarios, we introduced an additional constraint to the baseline problem. Specifically, we restricted the joint usage of Qwen1.5 and Deepseek-llm to a maximum of two instances. This constraint was designed to enforce a more even distribution of model utilization. Maintaining all other settings constant, we introduced this additional constraint and compared our method’s performance against the other benchmark algorithms.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">During this experiment, the hyperparameter <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> minimizer are set to be 2.5 and 20, respectively. The results are presented in Figure <a href="#A3.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ C.2.2 Robustness Check Under Extra Constraint ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F14" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.05340v1/spo_loss_curves_avg_llm_extra.png" id="A3.F14.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:286/238;" width="286" height="238" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F14.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 14</span>: </span><span id="A3.F14.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">SPO Risk Under Extra Constraint</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A3.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ C.2.2 Robustness Check Under Extra Constraint ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> demonstrates that, under the additional constraint, the testing set SPO risk curves are similar with the original problem. Our method continues to outperform other benchmark algorithms. These results indicate that our method remains consistent under additional constraints, demonstrating its robustness to changes in the downstream decision-making problem.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.3 </span>Empirical evidence of the Degeneracy Angle and Optimality Gap</h4>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To demonstrate the presence of the degeneracy angle and the optimality gap, we constructed various hypothesis sets to analyze their empirical distributions. Specifically, we generated 100 independent random hypothesis sets, denoted as <math id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}_{1},\dots,\mathcal{H}_{100}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mn>100</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}_{1},\dots,\mathcal{H}_{100}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each set <math id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> consists of five random hypotheses <math id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}^{k},\dots,h_{5}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mn>5</mn><mi>k</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}^{k},\dots,h_{5}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. We constructed each individual hypothesis by drawing <math id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> samples with replacement from each category—where <math id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> is drawn from <math id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\text{Uniform}[5,10]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Uniform</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Uniform}[5,10]</annotation></semantics></math>—and calculating the categorical sample mean. Figure <a href="#A3.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ C.2.3 Empirical evidence of the Degeneracy Angle and Optimality Gap ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> shows the histogram of the experiment result.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F15" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.05340v1/spo_angle_hist.png" id="A3.F15.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:238/190;" width="238" height="190" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A3.F15.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 15</span>: </span><span id="A3.F15.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">A Illustration of the Degeneracy Angle and Optimality Gap</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A3.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ C.2.3 Empirical evidence of the Degeneracy Angle and Optimality Gap ‣ C.2 LLM Allocation Problem Experiment Details ‣ Appendix C Experiment Details ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> illustrates the existence of a strictly positive degeneracy angle and optimality gap. These metrics are pivotal to the convergence analysis and comparative evaluation of the algorithms discussed previously. This empirical evidence substantiates our earlier theoretical assumptions, verifying that the geometric conditions required for convergence are met in practice. Consequently, the observed behavior aligns closely with the theoretical result.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Proofs</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Proof of Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5 (Risk Bound) ‣ 2.4 Risk Bound and Rates ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a></h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this appendix, we provide the proof of Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5 (Risk Bound) ‣ 2.4 Risk Bound and Rates ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>. The high-level idea consists of two steps. First, we show that when the slackness <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> used to shrink the nested hypothesis class is not too small, the true optimal predictor is safely contained in <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> (Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma D.1 ‣ D.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix D Proofs ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>). Second, we show that the specific choice of <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> in Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5 (Risk Bound) ‣ 2.4 Risk Bound and Rates ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a> satisfies the condition in Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma D.1 ‣ D.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix D Proofs ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>, which completes the proof.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that for all <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A4.EGx9" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A4.Ex25"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<p id="A4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Consider the above applied to both <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math> and averaged over <math id="A4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,\ldots,t\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,\ldots,t\}</annotation></semantics></math> to yield:</p>

<div id="A4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For any given <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in H_{T-1}" display="inline" H_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we denote the discrepancy between the conditional expectation and the realized excess re-weighted loss of predictor <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> at time <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup><annotation alttext="Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}:=\mathbb{E}[\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h;z_{t})-\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h^{*};z_{t})|\mathcal{F}_{t-1}]-(\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h;z_{t})-\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h^{*};z_{t}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>𝚛𝚎𝚠</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>𝚛𝚎𝚠</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>𝚛𝚎𝚠</mi></msup><mo In the subsequent proof, we will show that <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{h}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{h}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is a bounded random variable. Since <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h_{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h_{T}}</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded and <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h_{T}}|\mathcal{F}_{t-1}]=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h_{T}}|\mathcal{F}_{t-1}]=0</annotation></semantics></math>, we have that <math id="A4.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h_{T}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h_{T}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a martingale, and we can apply Azuma’s lemma to obtain finite sample risk bound.</p>
</div>

</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Before providing the proof of Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5 (Risk Bound) ‣ 2.4 Risk Bound and Rates ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>, we first show that the confidence set <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math> contains the true optimal predictor <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> at each iteration if <math id="A4.SS1.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies some conditions in Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma D.1 ‣ D.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix D Proofs ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma D.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, if <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sup_{h\in H_{t-1}}\left|\frac{1}{t}\sum_{i=1}^{t}Z^{\mathtt{i}}_{h}\right|\leq r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>sup</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>t</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>𝚒</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sup_{h\in H_{t-1}}\left|\frac{1}{t}\sum_{i=1}^{t}Z^{\mathtt{i}}_{h}\right|\leq r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, for any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\leq T-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\leq T-1</annotation></semantics></math>, then we have <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}\in H_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}\in H_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof D.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Proof of Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma D.1 ‣ D.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix D Proofs ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Since <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T-1}\subseteq H_{T-2}\subseteq...\subseteq H_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊆</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T-1}\subseteq H_{T-2}\subseteq...\subseteq H_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, we prove Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma D.1 ‣ D.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix D Proofs ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a> by induction. Obviously, we have that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}\in H_{0}=\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}\in H_{0}=\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Assume that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}\in H_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}\in H_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\leq T-2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\leq T-2</annotation></semantics></math>. Next, we will show that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}\in H_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}\in H_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Since <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T-1}=\{h\in H_{T-2}:\hat{\ell}^{T-1}(h)\leq\hat{\ell}^{T-1,*}+r_{T-1}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T-1}=\{h\in H_{T-2}:\hat{\ell}^{T-1}(h)\leq\hat{\ell}^{T-1,*}+r_{T-1}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, to show <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}\in H_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}\in H_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, it suffices to show that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{T-1}\sum_{i=1}^{T-1}\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h^{*};z_{i})\leq\frac{1}{T-1}\sum_{i=1}^{T-1}\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h_{T-1};z_{i})+r_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>𝚛𝚎𝚠</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>𝚛𝚎𝚠</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{T-1}\sum_{i=1}^{T-1}\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h^{*};z_{i})\leq\frac{1}{T-1}\sum_{i=1}^{T-1}\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h_{T-1};z_{i})+r_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Since <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h_{T-1})-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{\ast})\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h_{T-1})-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{\ast})\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, by (<a href="#A4.E8" title="Equation 8 ‣ D.1 Proof of Theorem ‣ Appendix D Proofs ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>), we have that</span></p>

<div id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p4" class="ltx_para">

Therefore, we obtain that</span></p>

<p id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Thus, we obtain <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{*}\in H_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{*}\in H_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.  <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\square" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\square</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>

<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof D.3</span></span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5 (Risk Bound) ‣ 2.4 Risk Bound and Rates ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Here we prove a stronger version: with probability <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, for all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(A)\text{: For any $h\in H_{T-1}$, we have $R_{\ell}(h)-R_{\ell}^{\ast}\leq 2r_{T}$ and }\sup_{h\in H_{T-1}}\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}\right|\leq r_{T}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">: For any </mtext><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">, we have </mtext><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic"> and </mtext></mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.167em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">sup</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></munder><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em">|</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup><mo fence="false">|</mo><mo lspace="0.167em">≤</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(A)\text{: For any $h\in H_{T-1}$, we have $R_{\ell}(h)-R_{\ell}^{\ast}\leq 2r_{T}$ and }\sup_{h\in H_{T-1}}\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}\right|\leq r_{T}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="r_{T}=2\gamma L\sqrt{\frac{\log(2T|\mathcal{H}|/\delta)}{T}}=\mathcal{\tilde{O}}(T^{-1/2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>γ</mi><mi>L</mi><msqrt><mfrac><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>T</mi></mfrac></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{T}=2\gamma L\sqrt{\frac{\log(2T|\mathcal{H}|/\delta)}{T}}=\mathcal{\tilde{O}}(T^{-1/2})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">We prove Claim <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(A)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(A)</annotation></semantics></math> by the chain rule of probability.
When <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=0</annotation></semantics></math>, the risk bound in Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5 (Risk Bound) ‣ 2.4 Risk Bound and Rates ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a> holds by the definition of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{0}\geq 2\omega_{\ell}(\hat{\mathcal{C}},\mathcal{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{0}\geq 2\omega_{\ell}(\hat{\mathcal{C}},\mathcal{C})</annotation></semantics></math>. Next, we assume that Claim <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(A)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(A)</annotation></semantics></math> holds for all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\leq T-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\leq T-1</annotation></semantics></math> and our goal is to show that Claim (A) holds for <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> with probability at least <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\frac{\delta}{2T^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\frac{\delta}{2T^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. In other words, for any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in H_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in H_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{\ast}\leq 2r_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{\ast}\leq 2r_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sup_{h\in H_{T-1}}\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}\right|\leq r_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>sup</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo encoding="application/x-tex">\sup_{h\in H_{T-1}}\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}\right|\leq r_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> with probability at least <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\frac{\delta}{2T^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\frac{\delta}{2T^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>. If it is true, by the chain rule of probability and taking the union bound over <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\in\{1,2,...,\infty\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\in\{1,2,...,\infty\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we will have that Claim (A) holds for all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math> with probability at least</span></p>

<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The rest of the proof of the risk bound in Theorem <a href="#S2.Thmtheorem5" title="Theorem 2.5 (Risk Bound) ‣ 2.4 Risk Bound and Rates ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a> is to show that Claim (A) holds for <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> with probability at least <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\frac{\delta}{2T^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\frac{\delta}{2T^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in H_{T-1}\subseteq H_{T-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>⊆</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in H_{T-1}\subseteq H_{T-2}</annotation></semantics></math>, since Claim (A) holds for <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\leq T-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\leq T-1</annotation></semantics></math>, we have that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{\ast})\leq 2r_{T-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h)-R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{\ast})\leq 2r_{T-1}</annotation></semantics></math>.
By the ”Lipschitz-like” property of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}</annotation></semantics></math> and the decreasing property of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have that for any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\leq T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\leq T</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
</div>

<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">It implies that the loss function <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h;z_{t})-\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h^{*};z_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>𝚛𝚎𝚠</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>𝚛𝚎𝚠</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h;z_{t})-\ell^{\mathtt{rew}}(h^{*};z_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> is upper bounded by <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L\gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L\gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, so we can apply Azuma’s inequality to the sequence <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}</annotation></semantics></math>. By taking the average of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have that
<math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}\right|\leq\epsilon," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></msubsup><msubsup><mi>Z</mi><mi>h</mi><mi>𝚝</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}Z^{\mathtt{t}}_{h}\right|\leq\epsilon,</annotation></semantics></math>
with probability at least <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-2e^{-\frac{\epsilon^{2}T}{2L^{2}\gamma^{2}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>γ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-2e^{-\frac{\epsilon^{2}T}{2L^{2}\gamma^{2}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>

class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\leq 2\gamma L\sqrt{\frac{\ln(2T|\mathcal{H}|/\delta)}{T}}\leq r_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo
