stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>T</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>T</mi></munderover><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{G}_{T}\;:=\;\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\big(\|h_{2}-c_{t}\|^{2}-\|h_{1}-c_{t}\|^{2}\big)=2\,\bar{\Delta}^{\top}\overline{\epsilon}_{T},\qquad\overline{\epsilon}_{T}:=\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}\epsilon_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p7.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p7.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Define <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{T}:=\bar{\Delta}^{\top}(\sqrt{T}\,\overline{\epsilon}_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mi>T</mi></msqrt><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{T}:=\bar{\Delta}^{\top}(\sqrt{T}\,\overline{\epsilon}_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>. By the classical central limit theorem,</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex70" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex70.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{T}\ \Rightarrow\ \mathcal{N}\!\big(0,\ \sigma_{\epsilon}^{2}\,\|\bar{\Delta}\|^{2}\big)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.778em" rspace="0.778em" stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.798em;" width="0.798em"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{T}\ \Rightarrow\ \mathcal{N}\!\big(0,\ \sigma_{\epsilon}^{2}\,\|\bar{\Delta}\|^{2}\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p7.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p7.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Thus, the event that the blind rule prefers <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> (or, equivalently, fails to eliminate it) is</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex71" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex71.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{\overline{G}_{T}\leq 0\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Big\{\,\frac{2W_{T}}{\sqrt{T}}\leq 0\,\Big\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Big\{\,W_{T}\;\leq\;0\,\Big\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">{</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><msqrt><mi>T</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟺</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn> 0</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\overline{G}_{T}\leq 0\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Big\{\,\frac{2W_{T}}{\sqrt{T}}\leq 0\,\Big\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\Big\{\,W_{T}\;\leq\;0\,\Big\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">By CLT, we have <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(W_{T}\;\geq\;0)=1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn> 0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(W_{T}\;\geq\;0)=1/2</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> goes to infinity. Thus, by continuity of the Gaussian cdf, there exists a constant <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\infty}\;:=\;1-\Phi\!\Big(\tfrac{1}{2\,\sigma_{\epsilon}\,}\Big)\ \in(0,1/2]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em" rspace="0.500em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\infty}\;:=\;1-\Phi\!\Big(\tfrac{1}{2\,\sigma_{\epsilon}\,}\Big)\ \in(0,1/2]</annotation></semantics></math>, (for example, <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.25</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.25</annotation></semantics></math>),
and <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{0}&lt;\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{0}&lt;\infty</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T\geq T_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T\geq T_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex72" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex72.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Pr(\overline{G}_{T}\leq 0)\ \geq\ \frac{p_{\infty}}{2}\ =:\delta_{0}\ &gt;0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>Pr</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.778em">≥</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>p</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0.778em">=</mo><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Pr(\overline{G}_{T}\leq 0)\ \geq\ \frac{p_{\infty}}{2}\ =:\delta_{0}\ &gt;0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Therefore, with probability at least <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> (uniformly for all large <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>) the blind baseline does not eliminate <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h_{2})&gt;R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{\ast}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h_{2})&gt;R_{\textnormal{SPO}}^{\ast}</annotation></semantics></math> under <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have exhibited a distribution for which the blind algorithm still retains a suboptimal predictor in <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, which proves item (2) of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Earlier stopping time than decision-blind design) ‣ 3.1 Comparison Under Optimality Gap Assumption ‣ 3 Comparison with Decision-blind Sequential Design ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>.  <math id="A4.Thmtheorem8.p8.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\square" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\square</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof D.9</span></span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Proof of Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Proposition 4.2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a><span id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
We first verify Assumption <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Preliminaries for Theoretical Guarantees ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>. By construction, Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> augments the hypothesis class so that, for every <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> and every <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, either
<math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(h(x))}{\|h(x)\|}\geq\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ν</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>≥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">η</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(h(x))}{\|h(x)\|}\geq\eta</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">or the prediction <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is replaced by a nondegenerate cost vector <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> corresponding to the cone that induces the same optimizer. By the definition of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>,
it follows that, for all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}\in\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}\in\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> and all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(\tilde{h}(x))}{\|\tilde{h}(x)\|}\geq\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>ν</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>≥</mo><mi>η</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\nu_{\mathcal{S}}(\tilde{h}(x))}{\|\tilde{h}(x)\|}\geq\eta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Hence, Assumption <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Preliminaries for Theoretical Guarantees ‣ 2 Algorithm and Performance Guarantees ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a> holds for the augmented hypothesis class.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">We now show that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> are equivalent with respect to <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> in the sense of Definition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Definition 4.1 (Equivalent Hypothesis Class) ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>.
First, consider any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math>. By the construction of Algorithm <a href="#alg2" title="Algorithm 2 ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, there exists a corresponding hypothesis <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}\in\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}\in\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math> such that either <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}(x)=h(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}(x)=h(x)</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is replaced by a nondegenerate cost vector lying in the same normal cone. In both cases, the downstream optimizer satisfies <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w^{*}(h(x))=w^{*}(\tilde{h}(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w^{*}(h(x))=w^{*}(\tilde{h}(x))</annotation></semantics></math>,
which implies <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(h(x))=R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\tilde{h}(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>SPO</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>SPO</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(h(x))=R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\tilde{h}(x))</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Conversely, for any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}\in\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}\in\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math>, by construction there exists an original hypothesis <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}</annotation></semantics></math> coincides with <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> except possibly at finitely many design points where <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{h}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{h}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is replaced by a cost vector inducing the same optimizer. Therefore, <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\tilde{h}(x))=R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(h(x))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>SPO</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>R</mi><mi>SPO</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(\tilde{h}(x))=R_{\mathrm{SPO}}(h(x))</annotation></semantics></math>.
Both conditions in Definition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Definition 4.1 (Equivalent Hypothesis Class) ‣ 4.1 Justification of the Directional Margin Condition ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> are satisfied, which establishes the equivalence of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathcal{H}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathcal{H}}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="A4.Thmtheorem9.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\square" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\square</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof D.10</span></span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold ltx_font_italic">Proof of Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem3" title="Proposition 4.3 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a><span id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
Let <math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{X}_{(j)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{X}_{(j)}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the corresponding design in Condition <a href="#Thmcondition2" title="Condition 2 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, for any suboptimal predictor
<math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∖</mo><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}\setminus\mathcal{H}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> we have</span></span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A4.Ex73Xe.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mu(\mathrm{X}_{(j)})\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]\left(w^{*}(h(\mathcal{X}_{(j)}))-w^{*}(h^{*}(\mathcal{X}_{(j)})\right)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>c</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>X</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>w</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>w</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mu(\mathrm{X}_{(j)})\mathbb{E}[c^{\top}|x=\mathrm{X}_{(j)}]\left(w^{*}(h(\mathcal{X}_{(j)}))-w^{*}(h^{*}(\mathcal{X}_{(j)})\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where the first inequality used condition <a href="#Thmcondition1" title="Condition 1 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, conditioned on any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> we have <math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x),c)]\geq\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|x],c)]=\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x),c)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mtext>SPO</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h(x),c)]\geq\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(\mathbb{E}[c|x],c)]=\mathbb{E}[\ell_{\textnormal{SPO}}(h^{*}(x),c)]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">By Condition <a href="#Thmcondition3" title="Condition 3 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and Equation (11) in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">El Balghiti et al. (2022)</a></cite>, for <math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1}=w^{*}(h(\mathcal{X}_{(j)}))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>w</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1}=w^{*}(h(\mathcal{X}_{(j)}))</annotation></semantics></math>, we have,</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex74" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex74.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[c|x=\mathrm{X}_{(i)}]^{\top}\Big(w_{1}-w^{*}(h^{*}(\mathrm{X}_{(i)}))\Big)=\mathbb{E}[c|x=\mathrm{X}_{(i)}]^{\top}\Big(w_{1}-w^{*}(\mathbb{E}[c|(\mathrm{X}_{(i)})])\Big)\geq{\eta\underline{c}}\underline{\gamma}." <p id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Consequently, by the lower bound of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> in Condition <a href="#Thmcondition2" title="Condition 2 ‣ 4.2 Examples of Optimality Gap ‣ 4 Justifications and Examples of Assumptions ‣ Decision-Focused Sequential Experimental Design: A Directional Uncertainty-Guided Approach" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, we have that the suboptimal gap is at least <math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underline{\mu}{\eta\underline{c}}\underline{\gamma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mi>μ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>η</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder accentunder="true"><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></munder></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underline{\mu}{\eta\underline{c}}\underline{\gamma}</annotation></semantics></math>. <math id="A4.Thmtheorem10.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\square" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\square</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
